entries.answer: An algorithm is a step-by-step method for solving a problem. When people compare algorithms they usually mean how the work grows as the input grows, written as Big O notation. An O(n) loop visits each item once; an O(n squared) loop compares every item to every other, so ten times the input means a hundred times the work. Choosing the right complexity is often the whole optimisation.
